import json
import re
from pptx import Presentation

pptx_path = "/Data2/v-weilinjin/workshop/AttributeBench/benchmarks/GAIA/2023/validation/a3fbeb63-0e8c-4a11-bff6-0e3b484c3e9c.pptx"
KEY_TERMS = [
    "crustacean", "crustaceans",
    "crab", "crabs",
    "lobster", "lobsters",
    "shrimp", "shrimps",
    "prawn", "prawns",
    "barnacle", "barnacles",
    "copepod", "copepods",
    "isopod", "isopods",
    "amphipod", "amphipods",
    "krill",
    "decapod", "decapods",
    "malacostracan", "malacostracans",
    "branchiopod", "branchiopods",
    "ostracod", "ostracods",
    "crayfish"
]

patterns = [re.compile(r"\b" + re.escape(t) + r"\b", re.IGNORECASE) for t in KEY_TERMS]

prs = Presentation(pptx_path)
slide_data = []
hits_by_slide = {}
unique_terms = set()

for i, slide in enumerate(prs.slides, start=1):
    texts = []
    for shape in slide.shapes:
        if hasattr(shape, "text") and shape.text:
            texts.append(shape.text)
    if getattr(slide, "has_notes_slide", False):
        ntf = slide.notes_slide.notes_text_frame
        if ntf and ntf.text:
            texts.append(ntf.text)
    full_text = " ".join(texts).strip()
    slide_data.append({"slide_number": i, "text": full_text})
    # Search for any matching term in this slide
    for p in patterns:
        if p.search(full_text):
            term = p.pattern[2:-2]  # rough extraction of term from pattern
            hits_by_slide[str(i)] = term.lower()
            unique_terms.add(term.lower())
            break  # record first term hit per slide

print("Extracted slides:")
print(json.dumps(slide_data, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
print("\nNormalized hits (first match per slide):")
print(json.dumps(hits_by_slide, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
print("\nUnique normalized terms matched:")
print(json.dumps(sorted(list(unique_terms)), ensure_ascii=False))
print("\nNote: Use hits_by_slide to count slides; unique_terms is only for descriptive summary.")

mistake_reason: The Verification_Expert misinterpreted the clearly labeled tool output by using the "Unique normalized terms matched" list (which summarizes distinct matched taxa across all slides) to determine the count of slides. The code’s stdout explicitly instructs: "Use hits_by_slide to count slides; unique_terms is only for descriptive summary." Ignoring this, the agent derived the incorrect slide count of 3 by collapsing duplicates of the same term across different slides (slides 6 and 7 both containing "crab"). This is a Tool Output Misinterpretation (FM-4.2): the agent incorrectly processed the tool’s output and treated a descriptive summary as the primary metric, leading to an undercount and a wrong final answer.
